findings.title: asked[run] is recorded when collect builds the batch, but step can drop that batch without printing it
quotes: When it prints the refuter batch it also adds the batch's finding IDs to the ledger's `asked[run]` (see Data model) and saves the ledger, in that same call.
The ledger records a batch only in a call that printed it
if redo:
findings.fix: Record `asked[run]` only where the batch is actually emitted: in `step`, right where it calls `refuter_pack`, and in the CLI `collect` command that prints it. Do not record it inside `collect`'s return value. Add a misuse test that sends a refuter file during a `redo`.

sources.situation: In `step`, `got = collect(...)` returns the batch lines. When a packed lens has no output yet, or a juror was invalid, `if redo:` returns the `next: re-run <lens>` lines. That return drops `batch` and never calls `refuter_pack`. Under CT-1, `collect` has already saved `asked[run]` with every pending ID. The re-run lens juror can then write `<gate>-refuter.md` refuting a peer's finding, and the next call applies it because `asked[run]` is non-empty. That is the forgery US-1 is meant to stop, and TC-13 does not test this path.

findings.reason: `step` (jury.py 1422-1435) calls `collect`, which per CT-1 saves `asked[run]` when it builds the batch. Then `if redo:` returns the re-run lines without calling `refuter_pack`. The re-run lens juror can write `spec-refuter.md`, and the next `collect` applies it because `asked[run]` is already non-empty. CT-1's rule "records a batch only in a call that printed it" is broken on this path, and TC-13 doesn't cover it.
findings.note: CT-1: collect takes ask (default True for nio jury collect, which prints the batch); step passes False and records the batch in refuter_pack, which it calls only when it shows the batch; TC-16 covers a refuter file written during a redo

findings.title: CT-7 drops the outcome check entirely, which goes beyond FR-10's rejected round
quotes: applies after any recorded outcome, `rejected` included, not only `approved`, `human` or `closed`
IF a gate's round was rejected, the artefact changed since in anything but whitespace
findings.fix: Limit the widened branch to a ledger with a recorded `rejected` round (plus the `rerun` that follows it), and say so in CT-7.

sources.situation: In the existing code, the fallback `rerun = set(votes(led))` runs only when `led["recorded"][-1][1] in ("approved", "human", "closed")`. CT-7 lets it run after any outcome. That includes a first review that was never rejected, where the empty set is currently left to FR-5's "show the human". This changes first-review behaviour that no requirement asks for, and the spec's non-goal rules out "Any refactor beyond the lines each fix needs".

findings.note: CT-7: the widened branch applies only at the spec, plan and tasks gates after a rejected round

findings.title: Every "show the human" call from the empty-lens guard leaves a new empty run
quotes: and no pack or `step.json` written
run = run or _reusable(root, slug, gate) or records.new_run(root)
findings.fix: Check for empty lenses in `step` before it calls `records.new_run`, or let `_begin`'s show-the-human line leave out `run:` and have the caller skip creating the run.

sources.situation: `step` creates the run before `_begin`, on both the no-output path and the `rerun` path (`fresh = _reusable(root, slug, gate) or records.new_run(root)`). `_reusable` only finds a run through its `packs/step.json`. Since CT-6 writes no `step.json`, each call (TC-8 makes three) creates and names another empty `R-…` run.

`step` creates the run (folder plus `promote.md`) before `_begin` sees the empty lens list. CT-6 then writes no `step.json`, so `_reusable` never finds that run again. Every repeated call (TC-8 makes three) leaves another empty `R-*` folder. The `run:` line also names a run nobody will drive.

findings.note: CT-6: _begin allocates the run only when lenses is non-empty; the show-the-human path prints no run line and creates no folder; TC-8 counts run folders

findings.title: No test proves a failed land's patch restores the work after the worktree is deleted
quotes: major data loss: a shelved or failed-to-land patch is the only copy of the work (#102).
for each of the four files the main tree's bytes equal the worktree's; the saved patch's bytes contain
records.git(root, "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(tree), full=True)
findings.fix: add a TC in which `land` fails (the main tree has a conflicting edit to `win.txt`), then `git apply --binary` the saved patch on a clean checkout of the base and assert that every file's bytes equal the worktree's bytes from before.

sources.situation: a wave task's `land` fails to apply (e.g. a conflict with the main tree). The worktree is force-removed and the `T-n.patch` is the only copy. TC-4, TC-6 and TC-14 test only a land that succeeds, so nothing shows that this patch, written by the new byte path, re-applies with the CRLF, latin-1 and binary files intact.

findings.reason: `land` writes the patch and then applies that same file (implement.py 368-373). TC-4 and TC-14 apply the saved patch successfully with CRLF, latin-1 and binary files, and TC-6 shows its bytes equal git's. TC-5 re-applies shelve's patch with `git apply --binary`. A failed apply doesn't change how the patch is written, so a failure test adds no proof of the byte path.

findings.title: A failed `git diff` still lets shelve delete the work after saving an empty or partial patch
quotes: the patch file is `git diff --binary`'s stdout through CT-4 with `raw=True`, written with `write_bytes` before anything is applied or restored (as today).
diff = records.git(root, "diff", "HEAD", "--binary", "--", *paths, full=True)[1]
findings.fix: in CT-5, have `land` and `shelve` check the `raw=True` exit code and raise before any restore, unlink or worktree removal. Add a misuse TC where `git diff` fails and assert that the files and the worktree are still there.

sources.situation: `git diff` exits non-zero (an index lock, a path git can't read). `shelve` keeps only stdout, writes an empty or truncated patch, then runs `checkout HEAD`/`unlink` on every path and force-removes the worktree, so the task's work is lost. `land` drops the same exit code and then deletes the worktree on the apply error that follows.

findings.reason: Ignoring `git diff`'s exit code is the code as it stands today (implement.py 368, 454, "as today" in CT-5). The spec asks only for byte-exact patches (FR-3, FR-4), and its non-goals exclude "Any refactor beyond the lines each fix needs". Nothing in the spec requires handling a failed diff, so this is a new requirement, not a flaw in the plan.

findings.fix: record in Decisions that a run in flight across the upgrade must have its refuter re-run (delete the file and call again), and add a TC that loads a ledger without `asked`, refuses, then deletes the file and gets the batch printed.

sources.situation: the old code printed a run's refuter batch and the refuter wrote its output. After the upgrade the ledger has no `asked[run]`, so the new code refuses that file. The only way on is to delete the refuter's work and run it again. The plan doesn't say so, and no test loads a ledger without `asked`.

findings.note: plan.md Decisions and CT-1 Fails: a run in flight has its refuter file deleted and the step called again

findings.title: TC-2's second finding merges into J-1, so there is no J-2 to stay pending
quotes: with logic giving a major finding of its own (built like `FINDING`, with another title and a quote from the fixture spec), so J-1 (testability) and J-2 (logic) are pending
same kind and the same cited IDs; near-duplicates are the refuter's `same-as`
where logic writes `FINDING` too (two findings)
findings.fix: give logic's finding another cite or kind in both setups, as the existing round-trip test does with `FINDING.replace("EB-1", "AC-1")`, and check after the first step that J-2 exists.

sources.situation: `add` merges a finding from another juror into an existing one with the same kind and cited IDs, regardless of title or quote. Logic's finding keeps `FINDING`'s `kind: gap` and `cites: EB-1`, so it joins J-1 as a second source. No J-2 exists. TC-2's "J-2's is `pending`" then errors or fails for a reason unrelated to `asked`, and the FR-2 filter is never exercised. TC-13 has the same problem: logic's `FINDING` is J-1 itself, so it never tests refuting a peer's finding.

findings.reason: `add` merges findings when `same` holds, which compares `kind` and cited IDs (jury.py 760-769) and ignores title and quote. TC-2's logic finding is "built like `FINDING`" (kind gap, cites EB-1), so it joins J-1 as a second source and no J-2 exists. TC-13's "logic writes `FINDING` too" is the same merge, so no peer finding is ever refuted.
findings.note: TC-2 and TC-13: logic's finding cites AC-1 with its own quote, so it is J-2; TC-2 asserts J-2 exists

findings.title: No test tells a per-run batch from any batch, so a forged refuter in a later run is let through
quotes: A `<gate>-refuter.md` not yet collected is applied only when `asked[run]` is non-empty, through CT-2 with `asked[run]`.
Setup: the first round's outputs, plus `.nio/runs/<run>/jury/spec-refuter.md` holding `REFUTE.format(n=1)` (#101's repro).
findings.fix: add a test where run 1 printed a batch and recorded its outcome, and a later run's refuter file written before that run's batch is refused with "refuter output before its batch".

sources.situation: TC-1 and TC-13 refuse a refuter file in the first run, when the ledger has no batch at all. A build that checks `led.get("asked")`, or passes the union of every run's IDs to `refute`, passes every TC. Yet in a re-review run a lens juror could still write `spec-refuter.md` before that run's batch and refute an ID an earlier run listed, which is #101 in round 2.

findings.reason: CT-1 says the file is applied only when `asked[run]` is non-empty, and the ledger keeps `asked` per run. TC-1 and TC-13 run in the first round, where `asked` is empty everywhere. A build that checks `led.get("asked")` or unions all runs' IDs would pass every TC, and no test covers a later run whose file arrives before its own batch.
findings.note: TC-15 adds a forged refuter file in a later (fix-check) run

findings.title: The batch is recorded as asked even when step never prints it
quotes: When it prints the refuter batch it also adds the batch's finding IDs to the ledger's `asked[run]` (see Data model) and saves the ledger, in that same call.
if redo:
return lines + [f"next: re-run {l} on .nio/runs/{run}/jury/packs/{l}.md, adding the INVALID lines above to it "
findings.fix: record `asked[run]` where the batch actually reaches the orchestrator: in `step`'s `if batch:` branch next to `refuter_pack`, and in the `nio jury collect` CLI path. Or have `collect` record it only when its caller says the batch is printed. Add a test where one juror is redone and a refuter file written before the batch is still refused.

sources.situation: `collect` builds the "## Refuter batch" lines and returns them; it prints nothing. `step` cuts the batch out of what `collect` returns, and when any lens has to be re-run (invalid output or needs-more) it returns the `re-run` lines and drops the batch: no refuter pack is written and no refuter is asked. Under CT-1, `asked[run]` is already filled at that point. The re-run lens juror, which has write access, can write `<gate>-refuter.md` for those IDs, and the next call applies it. That is exactly the forgery FR-1 forbids ("The ledger records a batch only in a call that printed it").

`collect` returns the `## Refuter batch` lines, and CT-1 records `asked[run]` there. `step` then cuts the batch out (`batch = got[cut:end]`). When `redo` is non-empty, `step` returns the re-run line and never writes `packs/refuter.md` or shows the batch. So `asked[run]` is non-empty while a lens juror is being re-run in that same run. That juror can write `<gate>-refuter.md` and the next call applies it, which is #101's exploit by another route. TC-1 and TC-13 don't cover this path.

findings.reason: CT-1 binds the `asked[run]` write to `collect`, which only returns the batch lines. `step` (jury.py 1422-1438) returns the re-run lines and never writes `packs/refuter.md` when `redo` is non-empty. So `asked[run]` can be filled in a call that showed no batch, which FR-1 forbids, and nothing else in the contracts settles this.
findings.note: same as J-1: CT-1 records the batch only where it is shown

findings.title: CT-7 bypasses the implementation gate's conformance-only re-run
quotes: applies after any recorded outcome, `rejected` included, not only `approved`, `human` or `closed`.
if (ids and not rerun) or any(awaits_fix_verdict(f) and any(s["lens"] == "cli" for s in f["sources"]) for f in led["findings"]):
and when nothing else would start the round the fixes need (CT-20)
findings.fix: limit CT-7's widened branch to the spec, plan and tasks gates (`gate in GATES`), or state and justify the new implementation-gate behaviour; add a test for whichever is chosen.

sources.situation: at an implementation gate, `diff` returns the files changed since the judged commit as `ids`. Today, a rejected round whose code changed with no lens holding a fix re-runs only `conformance`. Under CT-7, `rerun = set(votes(led))` runs first, so `ids and not rerun` is never true: every voting lens re-runs after each implementation rejection that changed code, and the CT-20 branch becomes dead code. The plan doesn't mention the implementation gate. The spec's non-goal says "Any refactor beyond the lines each fix needs".

findings.reason: In `changed` (jury.py 451-462), a rejected round leaves `rerun` empty when no lens holds a fix. Today only the conformance-only branch (`ids and not rerun`) then fires. CT-7 widens line 456 to `rejected`, so `rerun = set(votes(led))` fills first and that branch becomes dead for changed code. The spec files mention the implementation gate only in a test setup (tests.md:93), and nothing states or justifies the new behaviour.
findings.note: same as J-2: the implementation gate keeps its conformance re-run

findings.title: shelve's empty patch default is still a str
quotes: written with `write_bytes` before anything is applied or restored (as today).
diff = ""
findings.fix: have CT-5 make the default `b""`, and the same for `land`'s `(0, "", "")` fallback if it is ever written.

sources.situation: when no path is kept, `shelve` writes `diff`, which stays `""`. CT-5 only says to switch to `write_bytes` and to read stdout through `raw=True`; it doesn't change the default. `write_bytes("")` raises TypeError, so a task with nothing to shelve would crash.

`shelve` sets `diff = ""` and fills it only when there are changed paths. With CT-5's `path.write_bytes(diff)`, a shelve with nothing to save raises TypeError instead of writing an empty patch. CT-5 says it returns "as today".

findings.title: CT-6 prints a run that holds nothing, and makes a new one on every call
quotes: with an empty `lenses`, `["run: <run>", "next: show the human: the <gate> changed but no lens has a fix to check"]`, and no pack or `step.json` written
fresh = _reusable(root, slug, gate) or records.new_run(root)
(run / "promote.md").write_text(f"# Memory candidates for {rid}\n")
findings.fix: in `step`, compute the lenses to re-run first and allocate a run only when the list is non-empty. Or have CT-6 print no `run:` line and say the empty run is left behind on purpose.

sources.situation: `step` creates a run with `records.new_run` before `_begin` sees the empty lens list. With no `step.json`, `_reusable` never finds that run again. So each call in the AC-8 state (TC-8 makes three) leaves a new `.nio/runs/R-*` holding only `promote.md`, and prints a `run:` line for a run in which nothing will happen.

findings.title: CT-4's `raw` changes the return shape regardless of `full`
quotes: with `raw`, `(exit code, stdout as bytes, stderr decoded with errors="replace")`; without it, exactly as today.
"""git's stdout lines; with `full`, (exit code, stdout, stderr), for a caller that must see git fail (CT-19)."""
findings.fix: say `raw` applies only with `full=True` (`(code, bytes, str)`), or that `raw` implies `full`.

sources.situation: in the existing `git`, the tuple shape is `full`'s job. CT-4 gives the tuple to `raw` too, so `raw=True, full=False` has two possible readings: bytes lines, or the tuple. Both CT-5 callers pass `full=True`, so the contract only needs to cover that case.
